title: Plain-language soil and microbe benefits glossary

benefit_cards.plain_language: Soil microbes help turn dead leaves, roots, and organic matter into plant-available nutrients.
benefit_cards.look_for: Nitrogen cycling, phosphorus cycling, sulfur cycling, decomposer functions.

benefit_cards.plain_language: Some soil conditions favor microbes and fungi that help roots explore soil, handle stress, and access nutrients.
benefit_cards.look_for: Rhizosphere activity, phosphorus cycling, stress tolerance, transport functions.

benefit_cards.plain_language: Clay, organic matter, soil structure, and microbial biofilms can help soil hold water longer and recover after dry periods.
benefit_cards.look_for: Stress/drought signals, biofilm/motility signals, soil texture, clay, organic carbon.

benefit_cards.plain_language: Some soils protect organic matter better than others. Clay-rich soils and healthy plant roots can help carbon stay in the ground longer.
benefit_cards.look_for: Carbon decomposition, clay-rich soils, aggregate-building habitat, organic carbon.

benefit_cards.plain_language: Good soil structure helps water soak in, roots grow, and microbes breathe. Compacted or poorly drained soils behave differently.
benefit_cards.look_for: Texture, drainage, clay, organic matter, microbial habitat class.

benefit_cards.plain_language: Different native plants prefer different soil depth, texture, moisture, and pH conditions. Soil maps help choose plants that fit the place.
benefit_cards.look_for: Soil map unit, component, surface texture, pH, drainage, shallow limestone versus deeper clay.

evidence_warning_plain: This dashboard uses local soil maps plus regional microbial data. It can suggest likely soil benefits and microbial potential, but it does not prove which microbes are living in an exact yard or park unless local samples are tested.
